issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell after driving, wet spots or crusty residue near the top-center of the engine, or the engine starts to run hot. In bad cases the oil turns milky.
issues.why: The 3.1L V6 uses lower intake manifold gaskets that break down with age, heat and the factory long-life coolant. Coolant then seeps out of the engine or into the oil.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up and watch the temperature gauge. If the gauge climbs, pull over and shut the engine off. Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and check the oil for coolant; replace the gaskets before coolant damages the engine bearings.

issues.t: Water pump leak, coolant loss and overheating
issues.sym: Low-coolant warnings, coolant drips under the front of the engine, a sweet smell, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears and leaks. On the 2.4L Twin Cam the pump is known for failures and is hard to get to, so replacing it costs much more than on the V6.
issues.next: Don't keep driving with the temperature gauge high; an overheat can ruin the head gasket. Have the leak source confirmed with a pressure test and replace the pump. On the 2.4L, ask about replacing the timing chain parts at the same time.

issues.sym: A rattle or slapping noise from the passenger side of the engine, loudest at startup, sometimes with a check engine light. If the chain breaks, the engine stops and won't restart.
issues.why: The 2.4L Twin Cam from these years is known for timing chain wear and failures. Its small oil passages also make it sensitive to skipped oil changes.
issues.next: If you hear a new rattle, have it checked soon rather than waiting for the chain to break. Keep up with oil changes using the right oil.

issues.t: Ignition switch can overheat during long cranking (recall)
issues.sym: A hot or burning plastic smell from the steering column, smoke from under the dash, or the key and switch acting up after a long period of cranking.
issues.why: Holding the key in Start for a long time can overheat parts inside the ignition switch. GM recalled these cars (recall 02V-070 for 1996-1997 and 04V-036 for 1998) because a damaged switch could start a fire in the steering column, even after the car is turned off.
issues.next: If you smell burning from the column, turn the car off, take the key out and get out. Don't hold the key in Start for long. Ask a GM dealer with your VIN whether the recall repair was done.

issues.t: Ignition switch fails, melts or won't start the car
issues.sym: The car cranks but won't start or won't crank at all, the dash lights stay off when you turn the key, the key sticks, or smoke appears from the dash or column.
issues.why: The ignition switch on these cars wears and can short. Several owners had switches fail or melt wiring before the recall repair reached them.
issues.next: If you see smoke from the column or dash, turn the car off, remove the key and get out. Otherwise have the switch and its wiring tested and replaced, and confirm the recall repair was done.

issues.t: Airbags can go off without a crash
issues.sym: The front airbags fire while driving normally, at a stop, or even while parked, with no impact. Some owners also report airbags that did not fire in a real crash.
issues.why: Owners have filed many reports of unexpected front airbag deployment on the 1996 model. Some owners were told that water reaching the airbag sensing module, under the passenger seat area, can set it off.
issues.next: Keep the floor under the front seats dry and fix any water leaks into the cabin. If the airbag light is on, have the airbag system checked by a qualified shop. After any deployment, the airbag system must be repaired by a professional before the car is driven again.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy correctly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. The problem shows up only in a crash.
issues.why: A reinforcement in the instrument panel can break or snag the passenger airbag as it inflates, so it may not deploy as designed (recall 96V-211).
issues.next: Ask a Buick or Oldsmobile dealer with your VIN whether the recall repair was done.

issues.t: Interior lights turn on by themselves (recall)
issues.sym: The dome or other interior lights suddenly come on while you are driving at night.
issues.why: A fault in the interior lamp control can switch the lights on unexpectedly, which can startle the driver (recall 98V-027).
issues.next: Have a dealer check whether the recall repair was done. Until then, be ready for it at night.

issues.t: Underhood fuse box can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from under the hood, often near the fuse and relay box.
issues.why: A protective cover was left off the underhood fuse center on some cars. High current can then arc there and start a fire (recall 97V-059).
issues.next: If you see smoke from under the hood, pull over, turn the car off and get out. Ask a dealer with your VIN whether the cover was installed under the recall.

issues.t: Engine stalls or won't stay running
issues.sym: The engine starts and dies after a few seconds, or it shuts off while driving, often at low speed or when pulling away. On some cars the security light blinks.
issues.why: Owners trace it to several causes: the anti-theft system cutting fuel, a worn ignition switch, or fuel delivery and idle control problems. Many shops struggle to pin it down.
issues.next: A stall can take away power steering and brake assist, so leave extra room and steer firmly to a safe spot. Note whether the security light is on and have the codes read while the problem is happening.

issues.t: ABS light on, brakes grab or the pedal goes soft
issues.sym: The ABS warning light comes on or flashes, the brakes lock or grab on wet roads or turns, the ABS kicks in when it shouldn't, or the pedal sinks and stopping takes longer.
issues.why: Owners report recurring antilock brake faults and worn pads and rotors. Causes include wheel speed sensor faults and ABS unit problems, and dealers often could not reproduce them.
issues.next: Brake problems are a safety issue. If the pedal feels soft or sinks, don't drive the car until a qualified shop inspects the brakes. If only the ABS light is on, normal brakes usually still work but ABS may not, so leave more stopping distance and get it checked soon.

issues.sym: A light ticking or rattle for the first moments after a cold start that fades as the engine warms.
issues.why: Extra clearance between the piston pins and pistons makes noise until the parts expand with heat. GM documented this on these years.
issues.next: If the noise goes away once warm and the oil level is right, it is usually harmless. If it gets louder, lasts when warm, or the oil light flickers, have it checked.

issues.t: "ETC OFF" light on and cruise control stops working
issues.sym: The traction control "ETC OFF" light glows on the dash and the cruise control quits.
issues.why: This was a known false warning on 1996 models, and Consumer Guide reported no fix was available at the time.
issues.next: Have the codes read to rule out a real traction control or brake problem. If none is found, the car is usually safe to drive, but you lose cruise control.

issues.sym: A window moves slowly, stops partway, or won't move at all, sometimes after working for a while.
issues.why: The power window motors can overheat and fail.
issues.next: Avoid running a slow window up and down repeatedly. Have the motor tested and replaced; check the regulator at the same time.

issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel gauge, temperature gauge or tachometer drop to zero, swing around, or die all at once. Warning lights may stay on.
issues.why: The instrument cluster or its wiring on these GM compacts fails with age. This Skylark, Achieva and Pontiac Grand Am share the same platform and parts.
issues.next: Without a working temperature or fuel gauge you can overheat or run dry, so check fluids and fuel by hand until it's fixed. Have a shop check fuses and connectors first, then test or rebuild the cluster.

issues.sym: The front or rear hazard lamps don't flash when you press the hazard button.
issues.why: A defect can keep the four-way flashers from working, so other drivers may not see a stopped car (recall 96V-250).
issues.next: Test your hazard lights. If they don't work, have a dealer check the recall, and use other warnings such as triangles if you break down.

issues.t: Engine surges or accelerates on its own
issues.sym: The car speeds up by itself at highway speed, surges forward when put in gear, or idles rough.
issues.why: Owners filed reports of unwanted acceleration and surging under the throttle and cruise control category. Dealers did not find a single cause. The twin Buick Skylark has similar reports involving a jammed cruise control cable.
issues.next: If the car accelerates on its own, shift to Neutral, brake firmly and steer to a safe stop. Have the throttle linkage, accelerator cable and cruise cable inspected before driving again.

issues.sym: The air conditioning slowly stops blowing cold and needs recharging again and again.
issues.why: The evaporator inside the dash can leak refrigerant.
issues.next: Have a shop leak-test the A/C system with dye or a sniffer before paying for repeated recharges. Evaporator replacement means taking apart part of the dash.
